description:
The channel registry (TKT-235) is API-only. This story gives back-office staff the screens to
manage it: list, create, enable, disable, rename.

**Re-scoped 2026-08-10 (owner decision).** The allocation editor that was originally in this ticket
moved to **TKT-244**, because it needs an inventory credential that does not exist — see the
`kind=blocker` comment below and TKT-244's own description. What remains is reachable with
credentials the back office already holds.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A back-office channels page lists the organizer's channels — **enabled and disabled** — and
  supports create, enable, disable, and renaming the display name. The **code is read-only** in the
  UI: it is immutable per TKT-235, and a rename is a new channel plus disabling the old one.
- A disabled channel is visibly distinct from an enabled one, and can be re-enabled from the same
  screen. Disabling must not be a one-way door in the UI.
- Server refusals surface as field errors rather than a generic failure: a duplicate code for the
  organizer (409), and the write-gate refusals (empty/over-long code or display name, unknown kind).
- The page reaches catalog with the **`CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` the back office already holds**.
  It must **not** send `X-Internal-Token`, which the back office deliberately does not have
  (`compose.yaml:379-392`, pinned by `web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:471`).
- **Browser-verified:** `make browser` plus a spec in `test/browser/` that *submits* the create form
  and the enable/disable toggle — not just renders them. Note `scripts/browser.sh` provisions **no**
  staff account, so the spec must provision its own.

Quality gates: `make check` green; `make browser` green with the new spec; screenshot in the PR;
OpenAPI/types regenerated and committed before the gate.

Parent: TKT-17. Depends on TKT-235 (Done). Non-goals: the slot allocation editor and the inventory
credential (**TKT-244**); per-channel pricing UI; presale codes; the reseller API; any storefront
channel selector.

objective.note: Registry and allocations are both API-only; an organizer cannot split capacity across channels without curl. This is the story that makes the epic demoable.

scope.note: IN: channels list/create/enable/disable/rename-display-name, disabled channels visible and re-enablable, refusals as field errors, browser-submit spec. OUT: the allocation editor and the inventory credential (TKT-244), pricing UI, presale codes, reseller API, storefront selector.

uncertainties.note: Resolved by reading: registry writes are contract operations behind a credential the back office already holds; only the disabled-channel read needs a decision, and kind=blocker states it with its alternative.

dependencies.note: TKT-235 is Done and merged. The credential blocker moved to TKT-244 with the allocation editor; nothing this ticket needs is missing.

approach.note: One auth decision remains and is deliberately NOT deferred: reaching GET /internal/channels with the CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN the back office already holds, so the page can show disabled channels. Rationale and the rejected alternative are in kind=blocker. shaping.md keeps this owner:human because it touches auth — it is a much smaller decision than TKT-244's, not an absent one.

first_slice.note: One screen, one PR. The allocation editor is no longer in scope, so the earlier 'both screens together' argument no longer applies.

success.note: COS above; browser-submit evidence is the acceptance signal, per AGENTS.md.

binding.rule: Money is represented as integer minor units + ISO currency code everywhere; floats are banned on money paths.

governingAdrs.why: Channel codes are exact opaque strings — no normalization, no case folding; a registry must not introduce an FK from claims (historical attribution) nor a counter; release stays a clock_timestamp() predicate under the pool FOR UPDATE.
Catalog owns rule and entity definitions; commerce owns pricing/fee/promo evaluation. A channel registry is a definition and belongs in catalog.
OpenAPI is the source of truth; generated code must be committed before the gate or check-generate reads the regen as drift.
Response validation is fail-closed; a response that drifts from the contract is a 5xx, not a silent pass.
Staff identity and back-office sessions — the channels pages are staff-authenticated surfaces and inherit this session model.

reference.summary: PRD v1 — TKT-17 capability row + US-015 non-goals (registry/pricing/windows stay in TKT-17)
ADR-024 channel allocations — the shipped substrate this epic builds on
A web-UI ticket is not verified until a browser has SUBMITTED its forms — make check only renders back-office pages, so CSRF/checkOrigin, base-path rewrites, redirects and CSP are invisible to it
PUT /internal/slots/{id}/channel-allocations has no If-Match; ADR-024 accepts this while allocation editing is single-operator
The precedent for reaching a service directly with a per-service staff credential: COMMERCE_URL + COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN (TKT-194)
The allocation editor and the inventory credential were carved out here

governingTests.rule: Every file under src/pages/** needs a matching source:'page' row in ROUTE_MATRIX, and every row must name a file — a new page with no row fails the suite.

governingTests.test: web/backoffice/test/gate.test.ts:313 refuses a route no rule classifies
governingTests.rule: An unclassified route 403s for every role including admin — a page shipped without a matrix row renders a 403, not the page.

governingTests.test: web/backoffice/test/authorization.test.ts:244 uses only segment shapes the matcher models
governingTests.rule: Templates must be fully static, a whole [param], or a whole [...rest] — 'channel-[id]' is refused.
The back office must NEVER send X-Internal-Token — it does not hold the shared internal token. This is the ticket's blocker.
Every back-office credential must be set and must differ from the others; scripts/stack-env.sh generates each from an independent /dev/urandom read.
A refusal must be status-identical to an imaginary route and its body must not echo the path, the role name, or 'admin'.
test/browser/*.mjs is a glob with no allowlist — a new spec needs no registration, but browser.sh provisions NO staff account, so a back-office spec must provision its own.
Preflight checks storefront and scanner dist but NOT web/backoffice/dist, though Dockerfile.smoke COPYs it — a stale backoffice dist fails at docker build with a confusing error.

**Concerns:** 1. Blocked by TKT-235 until it merges (ordinary sequencing, not a risk).
**Verdict:** PASS — proceed once TKT-235 is Done.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=blocker -->
### ⛔ Not claimable as shaped — the back office cannot reach either endpoint this ticket needs

Found during the pre-claim `governingTests` bake (the context-mémo field added after TKT-235's
retro). This is exactly the class that field exists to surface: the blocker is stated in **no ADR**,
is invisible in the files a plan brief would point at, and lives in a compose comment plus a test
assertion.

#### The finding

TKT-236's two screens need:
1. `GET /internal/channels` (catalog) — the operator read, which returns disabled channels.
2. `PUT /internal/slots/{id}/channel-allocations` (inventory) — the allocation editor's write.

Both are `/internal/` routes guarded by `X-Internal-Token` == `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`. **The back
office does not hold that token, does not have a URL for either service, and is deliberately
forbidden from holding it.**

Verified at HEAD:

- `compose.yaml:379-392` — the back office's entire environment is `GATEWAY_URL`,
  `CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`, `COMMERCE_URL`, `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`. There is **no
  `CATALOG_URL`**, **no `INVENTORY_URL`**, and no internal token. The comment states the reason
  outright: *"that one value opens every service's internal surface, and this is a public-facing SSR
  process."*
- `web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:471` — pins the posture as an assertion:
  `expect(calls[0].headers['X-Internal-Token']).toBeUndefined()` with the comment *"Never the shared
  internal token, which the back office does not hold."*
- `web/backoffice/test/credentials.test.ts:14-44` — the two credentials it does hold must both be
  set and must **differ**; `scripts/stack-env.sh:55-61` generates each from an independent
  `/dev/urandom` read, *"A separate read, not a copy."*
- Inventory has **no staff-write credential at all** — only `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`. Catalog's
  staff-write credential exists but does not open `/internal/` (that surface takes the internal
  token, per `internalAuthorized`).

#### Why this is not a plan-stage problem

The shaping put `dependencies: met` because the only blocker considered was TKT-235, and
`approach: met` because the Astro write-form pattern is well established. Both were right about what
they looked at. What neither covered is that **the transport does not exist** — and the fix is not a
UI decision:

- Giving the back office `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` is refused by an explicit, tested, commented
  decision. It is also the precise mistake TKT-190 made and plan-review caught: one shared value
  opening commerce's refunds and inventory's operational holds.
- The in-repo precedent (TKT-194, `COMMERCE_URL` + `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`) is a **new
  per-service staff credential** reaching a service directly, in-network. Applying it here means a
  **third and fourth credential**, a new inventory credential class where none exists, and a new
  guard on inventory's internal surface — i.e. an ADR-043 question, not a screen.

#### This is stop-condition (b)

The run's terms say stop when *"implementation would touch auth … in a way the ticket and plan did
not anticipate."* This ticket's COS describe two screens; the work actually required is a new
service-to-service credential class for inventory plus a compose/credential-generation change. The
owner waived the gates for the epic on the understanding that TKT-240 was where auth lived — this is
an auth decision arriving one ticket early, in a story shaped as UI-only.

#### Options (agent's recommendation first, but this is the owner's call)

1. **Re-scope TKT-236 to the registry screens only** (create / enable / disable / rename). Catalog's
   *public* `GET /public/channels` is reachable through the gateway today, and the writes go through
   `POST /channels` / `PUT /channels/{id}` with the `CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` the back office
   already holds. Only the *disabled-channel* view needs `/internal/`, and a narrower fix exists:
   let catalog's operator list be reached with the staff-write credential it already has — which is
   its own small decision, but a much smaller one. **The allocation editor moves to its own ticket**,
   carrying the inventory-credential question with it.
2. **Split the credential work out first** as a prefactor ticket (an ADR + the inventory credential
   + compose wiring), then run TKT-236 unchanged behind it.
3. **Proceed as shaped**, deciding the credential design inside this ticket under the standing
   waiver.

Recommending **(1)**: it is the most reversible, it ships a demoable slice now, and it does not
decide inventory's credential class as a side effect of building a form.

#### Mémo updated

`governingTests` baked onto this ticket (below) — 8 invariants that would otherwise have been
discovered by failing the gate, including the `ROUTE_MATRIX` completeness guard (a new page under
`src/pages/` with no matrix row fails the suite *and* 403s at runtime, even for admin) and
`browser.sh` provisioning no staff account, so a back-office browser spec must provision its own.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=blocker -->
### ✅ Resolved — re-scoped on the owner's decision (2026-08-10)

The blocker below stands as filed. The owner chose **option 1**: re-scope this ticket to the registry
screens, carve the allocation editor into its own ticket.

**What moved to [TKT-244]:** the slot channel-allocation editor, and with it the whole
inventory-credential question — inventory has no staff-write credential at all, and the back office is
explicitly denied the shared `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`. That is an ADR-scale decision and now has a
ticket where it is the *subject* rather than an obstacle found mid-build.

**What stays here, and why it is unblocked:** the registry writes are **contract operations**
(`POST /channels`, `PUT /channels/{channelId}`) guarded by `CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` — a credential
**the back office already holds and already uses**. Nothing new is needed to ship the screens.

#### The one residual question, and the answer this re-scope takes

The page must show **disabled** channels, and today only `GET /internal/channels` returns those.
Two ways, and this ticket takes the first:

1. **Reach `GET /internal/channels` with `CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`** — needs `CATALOG_URL` in the
   back office's compose environment, exactly mirroring `COMMERCE_URL` + `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`
   from TKT-194. **No new credential**: catalog already issues this one to the back office, so the
   change is teaching catalog's existing internal guard to accept a credential it already trusts on
   its contract surface. Small, precedented, and reversible.
2. Ship against the public read only — enabled channels, disabling one-way from the UI. **Rejected:**
   an operator who cannot see or re-enable what they disabled has a screen that creates dead
   configuration, and "we shipped it crippled to avoid a compose line" is not a trade worth making.

**Why (1) is a genuinely smaller decision than TKT-244's**, and not the same thing wearing a
different hat: catalog's staff-write credential **exists**, is **already held by this exact process**,
and already opens catalog's *unsafe contract operations* — including the very writes this page
performs. Extending it to a read on the same service adds **no blast radius**: a holder that can
already create and update channels can trivially learn which channels exist. Inventory's case is the
opposite on all three counts — no credential exists, the back office holds nothing for that service,
and the surface it would open (`channel-allocations`) is a capacity write on the contention hot path.

**Stated plainly so plan-review can attack it:** this is still an auth change, it is still `owner:
human` on the readiness item, and if plan-review argues option 2 or a third way, that is the gate
working. What it is *not* is the TKT-244-shaped decision — that one is genuinely deferred.

#### Governing tests re-baked for the narrowed scope

Nine invariants remain (see the mémo). The two that most often break a plan that has not read them:
`ROUTE_MATRIX` completeness (a new page with no row fails the suite **and** 403s at runtime, even for
admin), and `browser.sh` provisioning **no** staff account, so a back-office spec must provision its
own.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claim — TKT-236 (US-CH2: Back-office channel registry administration)

**Selected because:** the owner re-scoped it today and cleared its blocker by carving the allocation
editor into TKT-244. It is now dependency-clear (TKT-235 is Done), it blocks TKT-244, and it is the
first child that produces something a person can *see* — the epic has shipped two API-only slices.

**Blockers:** none. `blocked-by TKT-235` is satisfied; the credential blocker moved to TKT-244 with
the work that needed it.

**Risk verdict: `risk:low` NOT claimed.** Two carve-outs. It touches **auth** — see the decision
below — and it is a **web-UI ticket**, which `AGENTS.md` says is unverified until a browser has
*submitted* its forms, so `make browser` plus a `test/browser/` spec is mandatory and `make check`
alone is not evidence.

---

### ⚠️ GATELESS RUN — the four gates remain waived

Same standing waiver, unchanged. Recorded per-ticket so this history stands alone.

| Gate | On this run |
|---|---|
| 1 — priority | **Waived.** Agent prioritized this child. |
| 2 — plan approval | **Waived.** Agent resolves open decisions after the cross-model critique: prefer the critique's recommendation, else the most reversible option; each recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 — review + merge | **Waived.** Agent squash-merges after the adversarial review converges. Review-guide posted first as the audit record. |
| 4 — PO acceptance | **Waived.** Agent self-validates each COS against evidence on the merged code. |

Unchanged: `config.models` routing with no substitutions, cross-model review for plan and code, TDD
with tests observed red or mutation-verified, `make check` green before every push and after the
merge, `make browser` green with a submitting spec, every marker comment, no AI attribution.

---

### The one auth decision this ticket carries, and that it is mine

`readiness.approach` is **`open`, `owner: human`** — deliberately, and it stays that way in the
record even though the waiver means I decide it.

**The decision:** the page must show *disabled* channels, and only `GET /internal/channels` returns
those. I will reach it with the **`CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` the back office already holds**, adding
`CATALOG_URL` to its compose environment — mirroring `COMMERCE_URL` + `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`
from TKT-194.

**Why this is not the decision TKT-244 defers.** Three differences, all checkable:

| | catalog (here) | inventory (TKT-244) |
|---|---|---|
| A staff credential exists | **yes** (TKT-191) | **no** — only `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` |
| The back office holds it | **yes**, and already uses it | **no**, holds nothing for that service |
| What it opens today | catalog's unsafe contract ops — **including this page's own writes** | would open a capacity write on the contention hot path |

So the blast radius added here is **nil**: a holder that can already create and update channels can
trivially learn which channels exist. That is the whole argument, and it is why this is a compose
line rather than an ADR.

**The alternative I rejected:** ship against the public read only, so the page lists enabled channels
and disabling is one-way from the UI. That is a screen which creates dead configuration an operator
cannot see or undo — a worse product to save one environment variable.

**How to disagree with me:** plan-review gets this as an open decision, not as settled direction, and
if it argues option 2 or a third way that is the gate working. The `overrides:` list at closeout will
name it either way. I am flagging it at claim time for the same reason TKT-237's contested COS was
flagged: an auth change settled quietly while building a form is the TKT-190 shape, and the point of
writing it down is that it cannot be settled quietly.

**What I will NOT do here:** give the back office `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` (explicitly refused in
`compose.yaml:379-392` and pinned by `web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:471`), or invent an inventory
credential. Both are TKT-244's, and reaching for either inside this ticket is exactly the scope creep
the split exists to prevent.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — TKT-236 (US-CH2: Back-office channel registry administration)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna`** via the codex companion (`task --model gpt-5.6-luna --effort high`),
per `config.models.plan`. Read-only. ~35 min — the longest draft of the epic, and it spent it
reading: the log shows it walking `authorization.ts`, `gate.ts`, `server_test.go`'s env harness,
`browser.sh` and both existing browser specs.

The brief carried the ticket, five COS, six governing ADRs, **thirteen governing tests**, and the
credential question stated as an OPEN decision with three options and an explicit "attack it" —
not as the orchestrator's settled direction.

# TKT-236 execution plan

Read-only review completed; the tree was not modified.

## Recommendation

Choose option 1, narrowly:

- Allow `X-Catalog-Staff-Write-Token` only on `GET /internal/channels`.
- Keep `GET /internal/channels/{id}` and every other internal route restricted to `X-Internal-Token`.
- Keep `internalAuthorized` shared-token-only at [`cache_control.go:69`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/cache_control.go:69).
- Make the pre-routing guard in [`server.go:219`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:219) recognize the staff token only for the exact method/path.
- Add `CATALOG_URL=http://catalog:8080` to the back-office Compose environment.

This is a credential allowlist change within the existing ADR-043 internal-route guard, not a guard-placement change.

The added capability is disabled-channel enumeration. Because `organizer_id` is caller-supplied, a compromised SSR process or token holder could query another known organizer; catalog authenticates the deputy process, not the staff member. The back office already holds a catalog-write credential, but the plan must not claim tenant isolation or tamper-evidence.

Reject option 2 because it publicly exposes disabled operator configuration. Reject option 3 because disabling becomes operationally irreversible from the UI.

Reversal cost:

- Option 1: remove one guard branch, the direct client, `CATALOG_URL`, and ADR-053; no migration or public contract change.
- Option 2: remove a public route and its contract/generated/gateway/client consumers, potentially affecting external consumers and caches.
- Option 3: easy to code-reverse, but requires manual API repair and fails the ticket’s acceptance criteria.

Record the decision in new `docs/adr/ADR-053-channel-operator-read-credential.md`.

## Roles

Admin only. This matches the existing catalog authoring routes in [`authorization.ts:64-73`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts:64).

`box_office` remains limited to the order console; `finance` has no configuration surface yet. Add the homepage link through `canAccessRoute`, while the route gate remains the enforcement mechanism.

## Definition of done

1. `/admin/channels` lists the session organizer’s enabled and disabled channels. Creation has an editable code; persisted codes are displayed readonly. Display-name changes use the existing full-replacement PUT. Code renaming is not offered.
2. Disabled rows have distinct status styling and an Enable action. The browser test submits disable, then enable, on the same row.
3. Duplicate code, invalid code/name bounds, and unknown kind are rendered beside the relevant field, with submitted values preserved.
4. Reads use `CATALOG_URL` plus `X-Catalog-Staff-Write-Token`; writes use the existing gateway client. No back-office code sends `X-Internal-Token`.
5. `make browser` includes a real Chrome spec that provisions its own non-default organizer/admin and submits the create, refusal, rename-display-name, disable, and enable paths.

## Files to create or modify

- [`services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:219`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:219) — exact method/path-aware pre-router credential allowance.
- [`services/catalog/internal/api/channels.go:77`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/channels.go:77) — collection-read dual credential; single-row read remains internal-only.
- [`services/catalog/internal/api/channels_test.go:225`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/channels_test.go:225) — credential, method, path, organizer, cache, and POST/PUT validation tests.
- [`services/catalog/internal/store/channels_smoke_test.go:163`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/channels_smoke_test.go:163) — add ADR-019 result-scope and exact-query `EXPLAIN` coverage for `operatorChannelsQuery`, asserting use of `channels_code_per_organizer`.
- [`compose.yaml:372`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/compose.yaml:372) — add `CATALOG_URL`.
- [`web/backoffice/src/lib/catalog.ts:26`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/lib/catalog.ts:26) — direct collection read, fallback URL, typed writes, runtime projection, and errors.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/channel-form.ts` — field-error classification.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/channel-page.ts` — pure page error normalization, including upstream 5xx handling.
- [`web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:1`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:1) — client paths, headers, malformed responses, configured/fallback URL, and no `X-Internal-Token`.
- `web/backoffice/test/channel-form.test.ts` and `channel-page.test.ts` — field mappings and page error behavior.
- `web/backoffice/src/pages/channels.astro` — new page with relative forms, `BASE_URL`, session organizer, readonly persisted codes, disabled markers, and all actions.
- [`web/backoffice/src/pages/index.astro:19`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/pages/index.astro:19) — admin-only navigation link.
- [`web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts:64`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts:64) — static `/admin/channels` admin row.
- [`web/backoffice/test/authorization.test.ts:62`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/test/authorization.test.ts:62) and [`gate.test.ts:281`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/test/gate.test.ts:281) — route classification and role refusals.
- [`scripts/browser.sh:38`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/scripts/browser.sh:38) — back-office dist preflight and catalog-container export.
- `test/browser/helpers.mjs` — shared `check`, database helpers, and stdin-only staff provisioning.
- `test/browser/reset-password.mjs` and `rate-limit.mjs` — use the shared browser helpers.
- `test/browser/channels.mjs` — non-default organizer/admin provisioning and all browser submissions.
- [`smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go:390`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go:390) — real-stack admin/non-admin checks and gateway edge denial.

No changes are needed to `scripts/stack-env.sh` or `web/backoffice/credentials.mjs`: no new credential is introduced. No OpenAPI or generated-code change is expected because the operator GET remains deliberately hand-mounted.

## Test seam

- Vitest: client headers/URLs, response projection, field mapping, page error normalization, route matrix.
- In-process Go: pre-routing auth, wrong-method rejection, HTTP validation, POST/PUT refusal behavior.
- `smoke/`: real Compose role enforcement, organizer behavior, and gateway denial.
- `test/browser/`: actual Astro form submissions and visual state transitions.

`make check` cannot submit Astro forms or observe SSR outbound headers. It cannot catch incorrect relative actions, proxy-aware Origin failures, `/admin` base-path mistakes, redirects/cookies, or stale back-office dist. The no-`X-Internal-Token` assertion belongs in Vitest, not the browser spec.

## TDD order

1. Add Go auth tests first. Before implementation, staff-token collection reads return 401; global or wrong-method authorization fails the negative tests.
2. Add client tests. Before implementation, channel wrappers are missing; existing code fails direct URL/header/projection expectations.
3. Add field/page helper tests. Before implementation, imports fail; incomplete mappings fail duplicate, boundary, unknown-kind, and 5xx cases.
4. Add the page and route tests. Before the matrix row, filesystem enumeration fails; before implementation, admin receives the generic 403 and `next` is not called.
5. Add homepage and smoke tests. Before the link or gate wiring, admin/non-admin assertions fail.
6. Add browser helper migration and `channels.mjs`. Before provisioning, no session exists; before each action, no successful POST or state transition is observed.
7. Run `make generate`, `make check`, then a fresh `make browser`.

## Risks

- `ROUTE_MATRIX` is bidirectional and fail-closed; the page and exact static row must remain one-to-one.
- `checkOrigin: false` makes `gate.ts` authoritative; every form action must be relative and browser-submitted.
- `browser.sh` provisions no staff account; the new spec must create its own account through the catalog container.
- Public `/channels` must not be added; internal routes must remain edge-denied and `no-store`.
- Full PUTs must carry the current code, display name, kind, and enabled state.
- The operator query must retain both correct organizer results and ADR-019’s physical index proof; output-only tests are insufficient.
- Existing generic invalid-channel text must be mapped using submitted values, while transport failures remain generic.

### Plan-final — TKT-236 (US-CH2: Back-office channel registry administration)

## C. Amendments

### C1. The tenant caveat is right, and the draft under-uses its own finding.

The draft flags that `organizer_id` is caller-supplied and that catalog "authenticates the deputy
process, not the staff member" — then still writes DoD-1 as *"lists the session organizer's
channels"*. Both are true and they are not in tension, but the plan must say which one the **code**
does, because they differ under attack:

- **The page must pass `staff.organizerId` from the session and must never accept an organizer from
  the request** — query string, form field or otherwise. That is what `events/new.astro` already
  does (`:56`), and it is what makes the caveat theoretical for *this UI* rather than live.
- **Catalog still cannot enforce it.** A holder of the staff-write token can ask for any organizer's
  channels directly. That is pre-existing — the same token already creates and updates channels for
  any organizer — and this ticket must **not claim tenant isolation it does not add**.

**Amendment:** DoD-1 says *"lists the channels of the organizer in the session, which the page takes
from `staff.organizerId` and never from the request"*, and the ADR states the residual plainly:
*deputy authentication, not tenant isolation* (ADR-021's rule about naming the adversary).

### C2. ⛔ The ADR-019 addition is out of scope. Drop it.

The draft adds *"ADR-019 result-scope and exact-query `EXPLAIN` coverage for `operatorChannelsQuery`,
asserting use of `channels_code_per_organizer`"* to `channels_smoke_test.go`.

**This ticket adds no query and changes no index.** `operatorChannelsQuery` shipped in TKT-235 and is
unchanged here; the plan is proposing to backfill a missing test for *someone else's* code inside a
UI ticket. That is the "incidental → new ticket" case in the skill's triage rule, and doing it here
bloats a diff a reviewer has to read.

There is also a real risk the draft did not notice: **the index it names may not be the one the
planner picks.** `channels_code_per_organizer` is `UNIQUE (organizer_id, code)`; the *partial* index
`channels_enabled_by_organizer` also leads on `organizer_id`. TKT-237's planner assertion cost a full
gate run to fixture correctly, and that was for a query the ticket actually introduced.

**Amendment:** removed from scope. If the coverage gap is real, it is a backlog ticket — and the
plan-final records it as one rather than silently dropping it.

### C3. The browser spec's own COS needs to be tighter than "submits".

The draft's DoD-5 lists five paths (create, refusal, rename, disable, enable). Good, but
`AGENTS.md`'s rule is about what `make check` *cannot see*, so the plan must name the assertion, not
the interaction:

- After submitting **disable**, the reloaded page must show the row as disabled **and still show it**
  — a filtered-out row would look identical to a successful disable in a screenshot, and that is the
  regression a render-only test cannot catch.
- The **refusal** case must show the message **beside the field** with the submitted value preserved.
  A generic banner passes a naïve assertion and fails COS-3.

### C4. Two things the draft's risk list should have named.

- **`enabled` on the PUT is a checkbox**, and an unchecked HTML checkbox submits **nothing**. Reading
  it as "absent → false" is right for a form but is the opposite of `ChannelCreate`'s
  `default: true`. The two must not be conflated; the create form and the update form read it
  differently and the plan must say so.
- **`browser.sh` exports no catalog container name.** The draft says the spec provisions its own
  staff account "through the catalog container" and separately proposes exporting it — those are the
  same change and it belongs in the DoD, not only in the file list.

## Pass 1 — 4 findings

### F1 [high] — Cross-tenant write. CONFIRMED, fixed.

`UpdateChannel` was scoped by `(id, code)` with no organizer. The page takes the channel id from a
**form field**, so a forged submit holding another tenant's id and code — the code is visible on the
storefront selector, the id leaks through any response carrying it — could rename, re-kind, enable or
disable their channel. **An id is not an authorization boundary.**

Fixed in the SQL, the contract (`organizer_id` now required on `ChannelUpdate`), the handler, the
client and the fake. The refusal is **404**, indistinguishable from a channel that does not exist;
all five states verified against a real PostgreSQL:

```
absent id, my org              -> not found
their channel, my org          -> not found     <- indistinguishable
my channel, wrong code         -> channel code is immutable
my channel, right code         -> nil
my channel, I claim their org  -> not found
```

**The gap shipped in TKT-235**, not this ticket — but this ticket made it reachable from a form, so
it is fixed here rather than deferred.

**The test I wrote first was worthless.** It passed against the in-memory fake while the SQL
predicate was deleted, because the fake does its own scoping in Go. The assertion now lives at the
tier the predicate does. Two mutants die there: dropping the predicate, and keeping it while leaving
the *disambiguation read* unscoped — which leaks "this id exists" through
`ErrChannelCodeImmutable`.

### F2 [high] — Renaming a disabled channel re-enabled it. CONFIRMED, fixed.

The rename form carried a hidden `enabled` using the **checkbox convention**, where absent means
false. But a hidden input **always submits**, so `value=""` is present-and-empty — which
`checkboxChecked` correctly reports as `true`. My own test asserts that helper's behaviour is right;
using it for a hidden field was the mistake. Now an explicit boolean string read as a literal.

**The browser spec could not have caught it.** It re-enabled the row *before* testing rename, so the
rename never ran against a disabled channel — an ordering that made the defect unreachable, in a
spec that looked complete. It now disables, renames while disabled, and asserts the channel stays
off. That assertion passes on the fixed code and is the direct evidence for this fix.

### F3 [high] — "The added blast radius is nil" was FALSE. CONFIRMED. See pass 2.

### F4 [medium] — Update refusals rendered against the create form. CONFIRMED, fixed.

An overlong rename flagged the **create form's** field and copied the attempted name into it,
sending the operator to edit an input that was fine. Errors now carry which row failed; row errors
render beside that row, create errors stay on the create form, neither borrows the other's values.

---

## Pass 2 — 1 finding, and it rejected pass 1's fix

> [high] Organizer predicate does not break the enumeration-to-mutation chain.

**CONFIRMED, and this is the important one.** After F3 I replaced "blast radius is nil" with "the
organizer predicate breaks the chain". Also false — **and I verified it by running the sequence
rather than reasoning about it again**:

```
STEP1 list victim      -> 200, 1 channels
STEP2 update as victim -> 200 {"display_name":"HIJACKED", ...}
```

Both `organizer_id` values are **caller-supplied**, so a stolen credential lists a victim's channels
and then mutates the ids it just learned, naming the victim in both calls. The predicate matches and
the write succeeds.

**Two wrong claims about the same guard, in two consecutive passes.** Both written in good faith,
both plausible, both false. What settled it was execution.

**What the comment and ADR-053 now say, and only this:**

- The read **adds bulk enumeration** to a credential that previously had to probe one guessed code
  per request via a 409, never yielding an id.
- It does **not add cross-tenant write capability** — the same credential already had it, because
  catalog takes the organizer from the request body and cannot check it. Enumeration makes that
  existing capability far easier to aim: amplification, not a new power.
- The organizer predicate **does** close the back-office **form** path. That was a real bug and is
  really fixed.
- Everything else rests on one assumption, which is the actual security property:
  **the back office is not compromised.**

**The chain is now pinned as a test that asserts it is PRESENT** —
`TestStaffCredentialCanStillEnumerateAndMutateAcrossTenants` — with a failure message instructing a
future reader to update the comment and ADR-053 and convert the assertion, **not delete the test**.
Same shape as ADR-021's rollback-gap test: an honest record of what is open beats a comment that
will drift. **TKT-245** owns the fix.
